processing: A cultivar rather than a finished style. Used for green tea, it takes the usual fixing, rolling and drying of the class.
harvest_season: Little is recorded for this cultivar. As with other Hunan green teas, the spring picking is the prized one.
appearance_dry: No description specific to this cultivar is recorded; a green tea from it would typically be a dark green twisted strip, possibly downy given its Fuding Dabai parentage.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Hunan green teas, a clear yellow-green; no description specific to this cultivar is recorded.
appearance_wet: Typically soft green leaf and bud, as with other green teas from Fuding Dabai descendants; no description specific to this cultivar is recorded.
taste_profile: No tasting record specific to this cultivar is available. Expect what is typical of a Hunan green tea: fresh and vegetal, with moderate body.

brewing.notes: General advice for a Hunan green tea, not specific to this cultivar.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under its own name; it mostly goes into regional Hunan teas. As is usual for green tea, look for the current spring harvest and drink it within the year.
description:
Fuda No. 61 is a Hunan cultivar selected from seedlings of Fuding Dabai, the famous big white tea plant of Fujian. The name is a breeder's label, and you are far more likely to meet it in a grower's field records than on a tin.

It is a shrub with a compact, even form. Its strength is yield combined with reasonable quality, and it does well in the climate and soils of Hunan's tea districts.

It does not travel equally well everywhere. In regional trials further north, including around Xinyang in Henan, its green tea came out slightly below the comparison variety and it proved weak against cold. That is a useful reminder that a good cultivar is good somewhere in particular.

Little is written about how it tastes as a single-cultivar tea, so brew it as you would a Hunan green and judge for yourself. If a seller names it, ask where it was grown.
history: Fuda No. 61 was bred by selection from the sexual offspring of Fuding Dabai and received provincial recognition as an improved variety from the Hunan crop variety committee for tea in 1987. Its breeder is not confirmed here, and little else is documented about its spread beyond Hunan and the trials in Henan.
